In order to accomplish our mission and objectives, we are required to collect, store and process personal data of our Subscribers, Hiring Partners and other Users.

Our commitment is not only to provide our Services, but also to secure your personal data in full compliance with the applicable laws in the jurisdictions we operate (collectively “Data Protection Laws”).

This Privacy Policy describes the privacy and security practices that OneGrow Learning employs when collecting, using and handling (processing) personal data and information about you in connection with our Services. It also explains the choices you have in relation to these processing activities.

Personal data or information means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data i.e. all information that relates to an identified individual or to an identifiable individual. For example, your name, address, or email address.

It is important to point out that we may amend this Privacy Policy from time to time. Please just visit this page if you want to stay up to date, as we will post any changes here.

In plain language, this means that: (i) you have to give us your consent freely, without us putting you under any type of pressure; (ii) you have to know what you are consenting to - so we will make sure we give you enough information; (iii) you should have control over which processing activities you consent to and which you don’t; and (iv) you need to take positive and affirmative action in giving us your consent. You can ask us to stop using all or some of your personal data by contacting us at support@onegrowlearning.com.
  • Right to access and/or take your data - You have the right to know what personal data we process about you, to receive information about how we process it and to receive a copy or summary of this data.   • Right of grievance redressal & to lodge complaint - We hope that you would always contact us if you have any concern or questions about how we process personal data or your rights with respect to your personal data. However, if you think that we do not comply with the Data Protection Law when processing your personal data, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the concerned data protection authority.
